What needs to happen is a comprehensive list of companies, their subsidiaries, and a summary of their track record. That way you can be sure you boycott most companies you dislike, not just the one that people talked about recently, and more importantly you can pressure individual merchants by not going to stores that carry unethical products. B&J (actually Unilever) probably doesn't give a fuck if you don't buy their ice cream, they'll just throw a few more million at marketing. But the guy running your local convenience store is struggling to break even, and he very much cares about wasting pressure inventory space on perishable product that won't move. And if people actually stop shopping at his store just because of this one product? Of course he'll avoid the hell out of stocking it.

In this case vocal minorities can have disparate impact as well. Even before people react to the unethical practices en masse, the fact that it is discovered could discourage the store owner from stocking it. From his point of view, even though the derogatory information is ignored by the consumer market now, it could go viral any moment, and then people will suddenly start boycotting, even if for a few days or weeks, but this means he'll have a batch of inventory going stale.
